summary: Created one evidence-linked defense and aerospace replenishment idea. European budget and investment forecasts plus RTX's current defense backlog, volume, margin, and cash conversion confirm the demand cycle, but appropriations, production, contract execution, commercial-engine liabilities, and valuation remain decisive. Enqueued one bounded RTX review; no relationship, strategy, signal, or paper order was created.

evidence.claim: EU member-state defense spending reached EUR 418 billion in 2025 and is projected at EUR 454 billion in 2026, with investment at 36% of expenditure and R&D rising to EUR 20 billion.
Collaborative procurement represented only 24% of equipment spending, identifying fragmentation as a concrete constraint on scale and supplier conversion.
RTX reported sales up 14%, adjusted EPS up 21%, USD 2.9 billion of free cash flow, and a USD 289 billion backlog including USD 119 billion of defense work, and raised full-year guidance.
Raytheon segment sales rose 18% and operating profit 29%, driven by land and air defense, naval, and air-and-space systems including Patriot, Standard Missile, and AMRAAM.

RTX identifies government-priority changes, program execution, export approvals, supplier constraints, product safety, and the Pratt powder-metal issue among material risks, so combined backlog cannot be treated as guaranteed cash.

daily_report_items: Researched defense and aerospace replenishment: budgets and RTX conversion confirm demand, but procurement, contracts, engine liabilities, and valuation block a strategy; queued one bounded RTX review.
